applicable_failures: Three full-store scan attempts timed out at 60s (calls 1-3), including the parallel range-split run, so no text scan completed and no intersected candidate list was produced.

The fallback was a filename/extension-prefiltered find (rwi|r&w|policy|binder... .docx/.eml, head -200), which can miss matters whose RWI content sits in differently named files; the agent's candidate list comes only from this filtered, capped output.

The self-assessed candidate list is hand-picked from filename hits; it omits matters in the unopened list (e.g., 1002-00001, 1015-00001 appear only as underwriting-agreement/IPO hits, which look irrelevant, and others like 1045-xxxx, 1005-00001 are unaddressed), with no sector verification.
critique.concerns: The stage goal (store-wide text scan with intersected RWI plus sector candidates) was not achieved. Every scan timed out and the agent never reduced the work (e.g., per-range runs in the background with output to files, or caching extracted text). The filename-only pool is partial and cannot establish sector. Many matters that surfaced earlier remain unopened.
critique.recommendation: Rerun the scan in background batches (nohup, per matter-range, writing extracted text to files), then poll for completion. Grep the extracted text for RWI terms and sector terms separately, with per-matter capped snippets. Build the candidate set from all matters with hits, and compare it against the filename list before moving on.

Common failures at this stage in past runs:
- After a scan that reached every qualifying matter, a follow-up filter on file names, document types, exact phrases or execution flags, or a cap on printed lines, dropped matters, and the candidate set was built only from the filtered or visible output.
- The scan itself missed matters because it was prefiltered by file name or file type, timed out, had a range filter that failed, or was read only partially, and the partial output was treated as the whole store without a rerun or a broader search.
- Scan hits listed matters that qualified, but the agent read only a hand-picked or number-ranked subset and never opened the rest.
- The script printed snippets for common terms across every matter with no output cap, so the output filled the context and no answer could be written.
What successful runs did: Passing runs kept the scan broad (all matters, documents plus emails), split it into parallel range scripts, or printed per-matter hit counts. They also kept the output to a manageable size, so candidates could be named from what the scan returned.
